Alright, I've ranted before about this. And yes, I am perfectly well aware that it is a rant.

We are not running out of Helium. For starters, the earth produces ~3000t / year from radioactive decay. Not to mention that we can in fact produce helium if needed.

The problem, insofar as it can be called a problem, is that we'll have a spike in prices when the US reserves that have been being sold at artificially low prices run low. That is all. It's not that we have a finite supply. We have as close to an infinite supply as we have of anything.

There's a huge amount of helium that gets vented from natural gas wells currently that could be collected, but it never made economic sense to do so in all but a few cases. (As usual: it is present almost everywhere, but is at a low enough concentration almost everywhere that most of the time it isn't worth it to collect it.) It is starting again to make sense to do so, but the setup costs are such that there will be a spike in prices until enough come online.

(Oh, and party balloons? Not particularly relevant. They tend to be filled with impure helium, effectively the waste of MRI machines / etc. And it's nowhere near economical to try and purify it currently. A better thing to push for would be to try to use higher-temperature superconducting magnets where possible. (Roughly speaking, the higher the temperature, the less boiloff required.))

I don't really own any video games where the focal point is an excessive amount of gore, but I do have games that feature gruesome or bloody deaths. After like 10 minutes I just had to stop. I will say that it is genuinely interesting to observe death. I think that everyone has a curiosity about it knowing that we all must experience it ourselves. But even so, I could only take so much of actual human death. There is a clear line of separation people have between their reactions to video game gore and real gore. We know video game violence is fake. We get that. It doesn't shape our views of what reality is supposed to be. You'd have to see real death to know what I'm talking about, but video games lack enough realism to effectively desensitize people to real violence. So basically, the people tweeting about how sick it is that people are cheering for the gore don't know what they are talking about. Also, lets be real here. People are more excited about the game-play itself. If a game had tons of gore but the mechanics were crap, no one is going to play that game.
